Smt Anand Prabha Agnihotri And 2 Others vs Union Of India
And 3 Others on 12 March, 2024

Author: Manoj Kumar Gupta
Bench: Manoj Kumar Gupta
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Court No. - 21
Case :- Writ - C No. - 7953 of 2024
Petitioner :- Smt Anand Prabha Agnihotri And 2 Others
Respondent :- Union Of India And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Raj Narayan Tiwari

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,C.S.C.
Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

Sri Divakar Rai Sharma has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of respondent no.2 (NHAI).
2. The petitioners have challenged the acquisition proceedings and, in the alternative, have also prayed for a direction to the respondents to pay adequate compensation to them for acquisition of their land under the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956.
Smt Anand Prabha Agnihotri And 2 Others vs Union Of India And 3 Others on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35267903/
1

3. It seems that at the time of issuance of notification under Sections 3-A and 3-D of the Act, 1956,
the name of the petitioners on the basis of sale deed through which they claim title was not mutated.
The petitioners filed objection at the time of determination of compensation and their objection was allowed subject to petitioners submitting evidence of their claim.
Notice of disbursement of compensation was also issued on 10.01.2024 by the competent authority in the name of the petitioners.
4. Counsel for the petitioners does not press the first relief relating to quashing of acquisition proceedings.

He presses his second prayer which is for payment of adequate compensation on the ground that the land acquired was non agricultural but the respondents have proposed payment of compensation at agricultural rates.
5. Counsel for NHAI submits that the petitioners have remedy of challenging the award under Section 3-G(5) of the Act, 1956.
6. We find considerable force in the submission of learned counsel for NHAI.

7. In view of availability of remedy under the Act itself, we decline to examine the claim relating to enhancement of compensation and leave it open to the petitioner to avail said remedy, if so advised.

Order Date :- 12.3.2024 AKShukla/-
(Kshitij Shailendra, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.)
